name: Plains
description: Flat grassland with few trees - the classic starter biome and the easiest place to build, farm and find your first village.
resources: Oak wood (scattered trees, often with beehives near flowers)
Hay bales in villages (9 wheat each)
Horses and donkeys for early mounts
Village loot: beds, food, iron gear, obsidian in weapon smith chests
whyGo: Best biome to start a world: flat building space, animals everywhere and a village head start
Horse breeding and taming
Bee farming: plains trees near flowers have a 5% chance to generate with a bee nest
tips: Mark village coordinates early - they are your first bed, food and trading post.
Lava pools generate exposed in plains: free obsidian and nether portal access before diamonds.
keywords: plains biome village horses bees starter

name: Desert
description: Endless sand, cacti and dead bushes. No rain ever falls, and the pyramids hide some of the best early-game loot in the Overworld.
resources: Sand and sandstone for glass and building
Cactus for green dye and defensive walls
Dead bushes drop sticks
Fossils generate underground (bone blocks)
Suspicious sand in pyramids and wells for archaeology (1.20+)
mobs: Husks (80% of surface zombies - they do not burn in daylight and inflict Hunger)
structures: Desert pyramids (4 loot chests + 9 TNT trap)
whyGo: Desert pyramids: golden apples, enchanted books, diamonds and horse armor in 4 chests - dig the side, never the center pressure plate
Gold-level loot without going to the Nether
Open terrain with no rain: clear visibility for building mega-projects
tips: In pyramids, mine down the side wall to the chest level - the center TNT trap destroys the loot.
Husks ignore sunlight: bring a shield at dawn.
keywords: desert biome pyramid temple loot camel husk archaeology

name: Jungle
description: Dense rainforest with giant trees, bamboo and vines. Hard to move through, but packed with resources that exist nowhere else.
resources: Jungle wood, bamboo, cocoa beans, vines and melons
Jungle temple loot and suspicious gravel (archaeology)
Ocelots, parrots and pandas
Moss carpets and glow berries in lush caves below
mobs: Standard hostile mobs under the canopy
structures: Jungle temples (arrow traps, puzzle chest, loot)
whyGo: Only biome with pandas and cocoa beans
Bamboo for scaffolding - the builder's essential block
Parrots mimic nearby mob sounds: a living mob radar
tips: Jungle temples: defuse the tripwire arrows before touching the chests. The hidden chest behind the lever puzzle can also be reached by simply mining through the wall.
Travel on the canopy, not the floor - it is twice as fast.
keywords: jungle biome temple panda parrot bamboo cocoa ocelot

name: Badlands
description: Colorful terracotta mesas and red sand canyons. The best gold-mining biome in the Overworld, with mineshafts exposed on the surface.
resources: Terracotta in every color (free, unlimited building material)
Red sand and red sandstone
Gold ore generates much more often and higher up (extra veins between Y=32 and Y=256)
Surface mineshafts with dark oak supports and exposed chest minecarts
mobs: Standard hostile mobs in caves and at night
No unique hostile mobs; husks do not spawn here (it is not a desert)
structures: No villages or outposts generate naturally
whyGo: Gold without the Nether: mineshaft hopping in badlands is the fastest Overworld gold
Terracotta farming for builders - bring a shovel and a silk touch pickaxe
Eroded badlands (the spiky variant) are one of the most scenic build locations
tips: Mineshaft chest minecarts here contain gold, iron, enchanted books and name tags.
No rain and no snow - fire spread is your main hazard near the wooded variant.
keywords: badlands mesa biome gold mineshaft terracotta red sand

name: Mushroom Fields
description: A rare island biome covered in mycelium and giant mushrooms. Hostile mobs cannot spawn here naturally - the safest biome in the game.
resources: Mooshrooms: infinite mushroom stew with a bowl, and milk them for mushroom stew or suspicious stew
Mycelium and giant mushroom blocks (silk touch)
Red and brown mushrooms
mobs: Mooshrooms only - no hostile mobs spawn naturally, ever
Monster spawners and raid spawns still work, so light is not the reason - it is biome-level
whyGo: Build a base with zero mob-proofing: phantoms and patrols can still visit, but nothing spawns on the island
Mooshroom farming for unlimited food
The ultimate hardcore-mode home base
tips: Bring dirt and saplings: no grass or trees generate here, and mycelium cannot grow most crops.
Phantoms still spawn above you at night - sleep or carry a cat.
keywords: mushroom fields island mooshroom mycelium no mobs safe biome

name: Cherry Grove
description: Pink cherry blossom forests on mountain slopes, added in 1.20. Beautiful, peaceful and the only source of cherry wood.
resources: Cherry logs and saplings (pink wood set)
Pink petals (renewable ground cover, bone-mealable)
Bee nests: cherry trees have a 5% chance to generate with a nest
Emerald ore below (it is a mountain biome)
whyGo: The pink wood set - the most wanted building palette of recent versions
Pink petals for decoration, renewable with bone meal
Usually generates next to mountains: combine the visit with emerald and coal hunting on the slopes
tips: Cherry groves often hide inside mountain rings with villages at the base - classic screenshot seeds.
Shear the leaves: they drop pink petals as you break them.
keywords: cherry grove blossom biome pink wood petals 1.20

name: Deep Dark
description: A sculk-infested cave biome below Y=0, usually under mountains. No mobs spawn naturally - except the Warden you summon yourself.
resources: Ancient cities: the best loot tables in the Overworld (echo shards, swift sneak, enchanted golden apples, disc fragments)
Sculk blocks for XP farms (sculk catalysts convert mob deaths into XP-storing sculk)
Deepslate and the ore veins around Y=-59
mobs: The Warden (summoned by sculk shriekers - 500 HP, kills through netherite)
whyGo: Ancient city loot: Swift Sneak leggings enchantment exists nowhere else
Sculk catalyst farming for XP storage
The ultimate stealth challenge
tips: Bring wool: walking on wool and placing wool around sensors makes you silent. Swift Sneak III changes everything.
Shriekers need 4 activations (within 10 minutes) to summon a Warden - break them after every mistake instead of running.
keywords: deep dark biome ancient city warden sculk shrieker swift sneak

name: Swamp
description: Shallow water, lily pads and oak trees draped in vines. The only biome where slimes spawn on the surface and witches live in huts.
resources: Slimeballs from surface slimes (spawn rates peak at full moon)
Witch huts (cat and witch spawns, crafting table + cauldron)
Blue orchids, lily pads, vines and clay disks
Mangrove swamp variant: mangrove wood, mud and frogs
mobs: Slimes at night (light below 8, Y 51-69, moon-dependent)
Witches in huts; bogged (poison-arrow skeletons) in swamps and mangroves (1.21)
whyGo: Surface slimeballs without digging to Y=40 - wait for full moon nights
Frogs for froglights (feed them small magma cubes)
Mud and mangrove wood palettes from the mangrove variant
tips: Slime rates are zero at new moon - check the moon before an AFK session.
Witch huts make compact witch farms (redstone, glowstone, gunpowder) with a small spawn volume.
keywords: swamp biome slime witch hut moon frog mangrove bogged

name: Taiga
description: Spruce forests with ferns, sweet berry bushes and podzol. Home of wolves, foxes and cozy log-cabin terrain.
resources: Spruce wood (2x2 giant spruce variant in old-growth taiga)
Sweet berries (food and fox bait)
Podzol (grows mushrooms at any light)
Mossy cobblestone boulders
mobs: Foxes (trust players who sneak-feed them sweet berries)
whyGo: Tame a wolf pack early - they fight for you
Foxes carry items in their mouths, including totems and swords
Old-growth taiga gives giant spruce: massive wood volume per tree
tips: Wolves teleport to you - tame 5+ and you have a mobile bodyguard.
Sweet berry bushes damage and slow anything that walks through them: free defensive hedges.
keywords: taiga biome wolf fox sweet berries spruce village

name: Windswept Hills
description: Steep, broken mountains with exposed stone and floating ledges. The only Overworld biome family with emerald ore and surface coal and iron in bulk.
resources: Emerald ore (mountain biomes only, Y=-16 to Y=320, most around Y=232)
Exposed coal and iron ore on cliff faces
Infested stone (silverfish) below Y=0 - mine carefully
Goats on jagged and frozen peaks (ram horns, 1.19+)
mobs: Goats (they ram players - keep distance on ledges)
structures: No structures generate naturally (villages can appear in valleys below)
whyGo: Emeralds for villager trading without raiding chests
Fastest early-game coal and iron: everything is exposed on the cliffs
Goat horns for signaling on multiplayer
tips: Powder snow on frozen peaks sinks you and freezes you - leather boots let you walk on top.
Falling is the main killer: bring a water bucket or Feather Falling boots before serious mining.
keywords: windswept hills mountains biome emerald ore goat powder snow
